However, a peer-reviewed evaluation published in the American Journal of Public Health and other research-backed sources directly refute this equivalence, noting that smoking increases the risk of dying from any cause by approximately 180%, compared to only about 25% for excessive sitting, and that media enthusiasm for the comparison has far outpaced the scientific evidence [d1][d9][d10].
